questions.question: A route serves files with `path.resolve(ROOT, req.query.name)`. Which check reliably prevents path traversal?
options: Reject names that contain the string ".." only at the start
Verify the resolved path starts with ROOT + path.sep
Encode the name with encodeURIComponent before resolving
questions.explanation: Resolve the final absolute path and confirm it is still inside the root folder; adding path.sep stops sibling folders like uploads-private from passing.

questions.question: Why is a regex like /^(a+)+$/ a security risk in a Node.js server?
options: Catastrophic backtracking on crafted input blocks the single event loop thread
It leaks memory because regexes are never garbage collected
It allows SQL injection through the matched groups
Node.js refuses to compile nested quantifiers at startup
questions.explanation: Nested quantifiers can backtrack exponentially (ReDoS). Since JavaScript runs on one thread, one malicious request can freeze every other request.

questions.question: Which change does NOT help against prototype pollution?
options: Using a Map or Object.create(null) for user-keyed dictionaries
Skipping __proto__, constructor and prototype keys during merges
Wrapping the merge call in try/catch
questions.explanation: Pollution does not throw, so try/catch changes nothing. Safe dictionaries, key filtering, strict schemas and --disable-proto all reduce the risk.

questions.question: Which command installs exactly what the lockfile specifies while skipping package lifecycle scripts such as postinstall?
questions.explanation: npm ci installs strictly from package-lock.json, and --ignore-scripts prevents dependencies from running install-time code.
